specification.title: A nested scope fails, and its ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails on the client
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API, on a pool of one connection.
Write the marker `outer`, and make sure the write was sent.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure the write was sent.
Checkpoint `inner-after-write`: report the backend PID. The runner sees the savepoint's subtransaction lock.
Arm the client-side fault (the next ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails in the driver and is not sent), then raise an application error in the nested scope.
When the fault fires, before the framework sees its error, the adapter's driver layer reports checkpoint `after-fault` (the backend PID): the runner records the fault's effect on the server.
The outer scope catches the nested scope's error.
Checkpoint `after-outer`, after the outer transaction's API has returned: report the same backend PID. The runner records whether that session is still inside a transaction.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: If the API reports that the outer transaction committed, PostgreSQL committed it, with the outer scope's writes and none of the failed nested scope's writes.
When the outer transaction's API has returned, the connection that ran it is no longer inside a transaction.

execution.description: DriverManagerDataSource. A connection is opened for the transaction and closed when Spring releases it. No pool. The outer TransactionTemplate uses the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED. A nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. TX-03 is not run in this mode (not-applicable-by-design). On this server, DataSourceUtils.releaseConnection closed a connection whose autocommit was false, and that backend was gone from pg_stat_activity. DataSourceTransactionManager.doCleanupAfterCompletion unbinds the holder and then calls releaseConnection, which closes the connection because it is no longer bound. The next TransactionTemplate ran on a different backend. This DataSource cannot hand a transactionally active connection to later work.
execution.form: Outer TransactionTemplate with the default PROPAGATION_REQUIRED, and a second TransactionTemplate with PROPAGATION_NESTED. Writes go through JdbcTemplate.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A client-side injection in the adapter's driver layer (node-postgres, pg.Client.prototype.query): ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT fails without being sent, as a failed send would.
fault.injection_point: The framework's rollback of the nested scope.
fault.preconditions: The framework's statements pass through the instrumented pg module (recorded as trace_sees_framework_pg).
fault.expected_server: The savepoint is never rolled back: the nested scope's write stays in the outer transaction.
fault.expected_client: An error from the nested scope's rollback; what the framework then does is under test.

knowledge: The framework knows that its savepoint rollback failed, so it knows that the nested scope's writes may still be in the transaction.

api_outcome.basis: TransactionTemplate.execute returned normally, so the template committed
api_outcome.contract: Spring Framework 7.0.9 TransactionTemplate.execute (org.springframework.transaction.support.TransactionTemplate) calls PlatformTransactionManager.commit only when the callback returns, and on a RuntimeException or Error it rolls the transaction back and rethrows that same throwable. The 7.0.9 reference, Rolling Back a Declarative Transaction, states the default rule: "In its default configuration, the Spring Framework's transaction infrastructure code marks a transaction for rollback only in the case of runtime, unchecked exceptions. That is, when the thrown exception is an instance or subclass of RuntimeException. (Error instances also, by default, result in a rollback)." The default tx:advice settings say: "Any RuntimeException triggers rollback, and any checked Exception does not." No custom rollback rule is installed. The nested TransactionTemplate uses PROPAGATION_NESTED. The 7.0.9 reference, Understanding PROPAGATION_NESTED, states: "PROPAGATION_NESTED uses a single physical transaction with multiple savepoints that it can roll back to. Such partial rollbacks let an inner transaction scope trigger a rollback for its scope, with the outer transaction being able to continue the physical transaction despite some operations having been rolled back. This setting is typically mapped onto JDBC savepoints, so it works only with JDBC resource transactions." DataSourceTransactionManager's class javadoc states: "This transaction manager supports nested transactions via the JDBC Savepoint mechanism."

error.message: Could not roll back to JDBC savepoint: injected client-side failure: ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT was not sent

evaluation.reason: TX-02.1 violated: the API reported: committed; xid 1202 committed at report time (`after-outer`); outer visible: true; inner (failed scope) visible: true

preconditions.description: the write of marker "outer" had reached PostgreSQL at `outer-after-write` (a row lock on item, in pg_locks)
the write of marker "inner" had reached PostgreSQL at `inner-after-write` (a subtransaction lock, in pg_locks)
the client-side fault (client-reject) fired exactly once
the nested scope's error reached the outer scope, which handled it
the runner observed the transaction's session after the outer API returned
the withheld ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT left the savepoint live: the session was in its transaction, holding the savepoint's subtransaction lock
preconditions.detail: at `after-fault`: session "idle in transaction", backend_xid 1202; transactionid locks [1202, 1203]
